{{Quote|The exiled leaders of the Church of Infinite Perception have reclaimed rule of the planet Pergitor in a bloody coup, ending what they call years of "liberal decadence."|[[HoloNet News/Legends|Holonet News]]|<ref name="HNN 46" />}}
The '''coup on Pergitor''' occurred in [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]],<ref name="HNN 46" /> shortly before the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. After the bankruptcy of [[Jesa Corporation]] the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] had been under the control of the [[Royal family of Pergitor|royal family]], which had imposed strict rules on the population and controlled the planet prohibiting open dissent. After 15 years of oppression the young began to rebel, [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] on the planet goods that had been prohibited since its colonization and starting a liberal movement on the planet that caused Pergitor's society to abandon its dogmatic rules and rituals for 15 years. In 23 BBY the [[Church of Infinite Perception]], taking advantage of the dissatisfiement many conservatives had with the laxation of the planet's new way of life, organized a coup to take control of the government. Lead by a man simply known as [[The Preceptor]], the Church exiled the royal family and established a fundamentalist theocratic dictatorship.<ref name="GG6" /><ref name="GG6.2" /> Thousands were killed by the Church durning the coup but due to Pergitor's nebulous affiliation with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], neither the Republic nor the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] could do anything to stop the bloody revolt.<ref name="HNN 46" />

==Behind the scenes==
The [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Pergitor]], alongside its history, was first presented in [[West End Games]]' [[Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters|Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters]]. Despite it not giving a precise date for the events it covers, Galaxy Guides are supplements to WEG's [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]] which is set in the years after [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope]] but before [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back]]. Dating the supplement to the time period of the core rulebook would place the coup between [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]] and [[12 BBY/Legends|12 BBY]].

On [[March 7]], [[2002]] the official ''[[Star Wars]]'' website [[HoloNet News (original website)|Holonet News]] that was created as part of the marketing campaign for the [[2002]] theatrical release of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] posted [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 46]]<ref name="HNN 46" /> featuring an article about the [[Church of Infinite Perception/Legends|Church]]'s coup on Pergitor, dating the event to [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]] and subsequently preponing all of Pergitor's history by about 8 years.
